records.issue_text: Capturing the request-derived ctx into the async index-init goroutine means cancellation of the constructor's context can abort the background index build, leaving a partial or missing index
records.rationale: The diff removes calling `Init(ctx)` from request handlers (e.g. in `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` the block `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` is deleted) and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` once in `NewResourceServer(...)`. So the index init is no longer driven by a request-derived context. The finding’s premise (“request-derived ctx ... into the async index-init goroutine”) contradicts these changes.

records.issue_text: Removing per-handler Init guards makes handlers like History and Origin dereference s.search with no nil check, causing nil-pointer panics for any server instance not built through NewResourceServer (e.g., tests, alternate constructors)
records.rationale: In server.go the per-handler Init() calls were removed from History and Origin, and both now directly dereference `s.search` (`return s.search.History(ctx, req)` / `return s.search.Origin(ctx, req)`) with no `nil` guard. records.issue_text: Removing the cacheMu lock around BuildIndex body creates a lost-update/concurrent-build race where two concurrent calls for the same NamespacedResource both build the index, corrupting or failing the file-backed build and orphaning duplicate in-memory indexes
records.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go` the diff removes the coarse `b.cacheMu.Lock()`/`defer b.cacheMu.Unlock()` that previously wrapped the entire `BuildIndex` body, and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end. With this change, two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same `key` can both proceed to build (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` for the same `dir` when `size > FileThreshold`) before either stores into `b.cache`, leading to duplicated work and potential conflicts/errors for the file-backed index path. The diff provides no other synchronization or singleflight mecha
